request.deadline: Three quarterly milestones over 9 months, July 2026 to March 2027
deliverables: Ongoing maintenance: bug fixes, dependency upkeep, security patches, and releases
Initial Plutus V4 support in the compiler and standard library
Improved JS/TS interfaces and documentation for Scalus components embedded in MeshJS, Evolution SDK, and Lucid Evolution
Foundational runtime components and reactive workers
Ledger rules and transaction-builder updates for new builtins, cost models, nested transactions, accounts, and guard scripts
Java/Kotlin integration including Spring Boot and Ktor examples
Cleaner integration paths with Cardano Client Lib and Yaci
Runtime chain follower and task scheduler
request.what: Fund a 9-month continuation of Scalus covering maintenance, Dijkstra hard-fork readiness, interoperability across JVM and JS/TS ecosystems, and a first scoped application runtime.

claims.claim: Scalus is described as an established open-source Cardano development platform built by Lantr Engineering over three years of continuous delivery.
The proposal states that Scalus is used by or underpins Gummiworm L2, Bifrost, SugarRush, Vela, and DID/DIDComm systems.
The proposal states that Scalus components are reused in MeshJS SDK, Evolution SDK, Lucid Evolution, Cardano Client Lib, and YaciDevKit.
The proposal claims three years of development with 4,642 commits, 32 releases, 12 contributors, and more than 20,000 monthly Scalus.js downloads.
The requested budget is ₳2,464,844 for 9 months, approximately $394,375 at a $0.16/ADA reference rate, with no contingency.
The proposal says it is a reduced resubmission from a prior ₳8.503M, 12-month proposal, with FTE reduced from 8.25 to 2.25 and several contested scope items removed.
The proposal excludes a standalone production JVM L1 node, full Gummiworm L2 integration, broad formal verification, and advanced devnet expansion from the funded scope.

The proposal asserts that Dijkstra readiness is needed because Plutus V4, nested transactions, guard script types, and accounts affect contract development, evaluation, transaction building, ledger rules, testing, and workflows.
The proposal states delivery will be milestone-based and administered through audited SundaeSwap treasury contracts with an independent oversight board and third-party assurance.

The proposal argues that Scalus aligns with Cardano 2030 by enabling developer infrastructure, interoperability, education, and ecosystem growth rather than directly producing TVL, transactions, or active users itself.

summary: The document requests ₳2,464,844 for Lantr Engineering to continue Scalus over July 2026 to March 2027, emphasizing maintenance, Dijkstra readiness, interoperability, and a scoped runtime while presenting adoption, prior delivery, reduced scope, and governance controls as the main justification.
